Yes, you must provide samples of your pigment and the finished eyeshadow if FDA requests them, as the Commissioner has the authority to request such samples during the review of a color additive petition. The request for samples does affect the review timeline: the date used for computing the 90-day limit shall be moved forward one day for each day taken by the petitioner to submit the information and/or sample after the mailing date of the request. If the information or sample is requested a reasonable time in advance of the 180 days, but is not submitted within such 180 days after filing of the petition, the petition will be considered withdrawn without prejudice.

21 CFR 71.4 requires that the Commissioner may request samples of the color additive, articles used as components thereof, or of the food, drug, or cosmetic in which the color additive is proposed to be used, or which comprises the color additive, and any additional information needed to clarify a submitted method or other aspect of a petition while the petition is under consideration [1].  

The Commissioner shall specify in the request for a sample a quantity deemed adequate to permit tests of analytical methods to determine quantities of the color additive present in products for which it is intended to be used, or adequate for any study or investigation reasonably required with respect to the safety of the color additive or the physical or technical effect it produces [1].  

The date used for computing the 90-day limit shall be moved forward one day for each day taken by the petitioner to submit the information and/or sample after the mailing date of the request [1].
